messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] Sev2 - Serving runtime error spike - cluster: eu-west-1-serving - 5xx and crashloops increasing. AutoScale events spiking -> rapid add/remove causing node flaps. Affected: model-serving pool (gpu-rt). Pager routed to oncall.
oncall-alex: Acked. jumping in. seeing the alerts in console. cuDA OOM + CrashLoopBackOff on ~12 pods. autoscaler reports +80 -> -70 replicas in last 8m.
sre-maya: grabbing logs now. I see repeated: \"CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: Tried to allocate 2.5GB on GPU 0\" then container exits with SIGABRT. Also kubelet complaining about eviction thrash.
eng-runtime-jordan: this pattern matches continuous batching growth + cache warming after scale-up. batch sizes ballooning with new nodes, then memory spike. suspect autoscaler too aggressive.
oncall-alex: immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause autoscale (set target replicas to a safe fixed value) 2) roll failing pods to a smaller model variant / quantized 3) route some traffic to fallback region 4) dampen scale-down to avoid oscillation.
infra-ops-lin: I can set cluster autoscaler disabled for the pool. Recommend setting max surge and scale-down delay. Running: 
```bash
# disable CA for the node group temporarily
kubectl annotate nodegroup gpu-serving cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled=true --overwrite
```
(oncall) Alex: good, do that. also pin HPA min to 8 to stop ripples.
sre-maya: patching HPA now: 
```bash
kubectl patch hpa gpu-serving -p '{"spec": {"minReplicas": 8, "behavior": {"scaleDown": {"stabilizationWindowSeconds": 600}}}}'
```
(small delay) patch applied. scale-down stabilization set to 10m.
eng-runtime-jordan: pushing a config to runtime to cap continuous batching to 8 items and reduce KV cache prefetch. Deploying safe config: 
```yaml
serving:
  max_batch_size: 8
  kv_cache_prefetch: false
```
Applying now.
sre-maya: restarting crashloop pods one-by-one to avoid mass scheduling to new nodes. `kubectl rollout restart deployment/gpu-serving -n inference --field-selector metadata.name=gpu-serving` (serial).
oncall-alex: product-ops-zoe, any customer-facing impact?
product-ops-zoe: some customers on EU are seeing elevated latency and 502s for 5-10m windows. CS has a handful of tickets for timeouts. No broad data loss. I'm drafting status note: "We’re mitigating an infrastructure scaling issue causing transient errors and elevated latency; working on restoring normal traffic routing."
infra-ops-lin: cordoned two flapping nodes (ip-10-0-4-21, ip-10-0-4-33) to prevent rescheduling during investigation: `kubectl cordon <node>` done.
sre-maya: after capping batch, crashloops decreased. Current pod restarts dropping from ~3/min to 0.2/min. GPU memory pressure trending down.
eng-runtime-jordan: I can serve a quantized v2 variant (q8) for a short window to reduce memory footprint. Recommend routing 50% traffic to q8 for EU while we validate. How to do weighted rollout?
sre-maya: we can patch service route weights in the router: 
```bash
routerctl set-weight model-v2:q8 0.5 --namespace eu-west-1
```
Done. Traffic split configured.
oncall-alex: Good. Monitoring. Can we also prevent the autoscaler from reacting to our temporary traffic shift?
infra-ops-lin: set autoscaler to ignore sudden CPU/GPU burst signals by switching to custom metric smoothing: `kubectl apply -f neat-autoscaler-config.yaml` - applied.
product-ops-zoe: sending an interim customer update now. I'll link to status page.
sre-maya: note: I still see occasional CUDA OOMs coming from one specific node; investigating GPU driver logs.
eng-runtime-jordan: let's isolate that node and repro locally. may be a driver mismatch introduced in latest node image. If confirmed, we'll evict and reprovision.
infra-ops-lin: node reprovision queued. evicting pods gracefully from ip-10-0-4-21.
incident-bot: Status update - incident state: mitigation in-progress. Impact: partial latency increase and transient 5xx for eu-west-1; affected customers limited. CI run: autoscaler paused, batch cap applied, q8 fallback routing 50%.
noncall? (typo) oncall-alex: update: CPU/GPU utilization stable at ~60% after changes. Crashloops nearly gone. Holding until next 30m to confirm no rebound.
sre-maya: checklist: 
- [x] pause/dampen autoscale
- [x] cap batching and disable prefetch
- [x] route 50% to q8 variant
- [x] cordon bad nodes + reprovision
- [x] restart pods serially
- [ ] monitor for 30m
- [ ] postmortem + runbook updates (assigned: eng-runtime-jordan)
eng-runtime-jordan: I'll own postmortem and follow-up: reduce default autoscale aggressiveness, add hard caps to batch growth on scale-up, add health-check to detect CUDA OOM pattern and trigger safe fallback automatically.
product-ops-zoe: customers notified. CS queued more detailed emails for affected enterprise accounts.
oncall-alex: Thanks team. If anything regresses, ping this thread and I'll re-escalate. For now we move to monitoring state.
incident-bot: Incident resolved -> monitoring. Duration: ~18m active mitigation.
product-ops-zoe: filing a short status update to blog/status page and closing the urgent customer callbacks.
eng-runtime-jordan: starting postmortem draft now, will include timeline and proposed fixes.
sre-maya: leaving notes on runbook: add a step to temporarily cap HPA and set stabilizationWindowSeconds when rapid add/remove detected.
oncall-alex: handoff to next oncall in 45m; leaving channel open for any regression. :thumbsup:
